name: Grandmother's Eye-Wash
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: clear, cold rain-water
ingredients.originalText: one quart of clear, cold rain-water

ingredients.name: sulphate of zinc (white vitrol)
ingredients.originalText: half an ounce of sulphate of zinc (white vitrol)

instructions.text: break the eggs into one quart of clear, cold rain-water
bring to a boil on a slow fire, stirring often
add half an ounce of sulphate of zinc (white vitrol)
continue the boiling for two minutes, then set it off the fire
Take the curd that settles at the bottom of this and apply to the eye at night with a bandage
Strain the liquid through a cloth and use for bathing the eyes occasionally

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. break the eggs into one quart of clear, cold rain-water
2. stir until thoroughly mixed
3. bring to a boil on a slow fire, stirring often
4. add half an ounce of sulphate of zinc (white vitrol)
5. continue the boiling for two minutes, then set it off the fire
6. Take the curd that settles at the bottom of this and apply to the eye at night with a bandage
7. Strain the liquid through a cloth and use for bathing the eyes occasionally
